topics.title: The hook: two coins, two ways to win
topics.why_now: The whole market got hit on Nov 5, and that is exactly when fans of a coin want to hear why they are still right.
topics.angle: Your face, big energy, what is at stake. Tell the Quant holders and the Kaspa holders that this video is for them.

prompts: Two coins. Two completely different ways to win. One is the layer the nation's largest financial institutions are letting into the building. The other is a coin nobody owns and nobody was handed.
inspiring: If you hold either one of these, this video is for you. Everybody is staring at the red candles, and I'm going to show you what's getting stronger underneath them.

topics.title: We are here: the 2023 chart
topics.why_now: Bitcoin rallied hard off its low, pulled back, and everybody flipped to fear. It looks a lot like early 2023, except that M2 is at a record this time.
topics.angle: The chart moment of the video. Scroll back to early 2023, circle it, say 'we are here', then come back to this week. It is the same move and the same mood, with more liquidity behind it. This is about the move and the money, not the calendar.

tabs.label: BTC weekly on TradingView
prompts: Look at this. This is early 2023. A big rally off the low, everybody gets excited, then a pullback and everybody panics. We are here.
Back then Bitcoin rallied 57% and pulled back 19%. This time it rallied 48% and we're down 12%. And here's the difference: back then M2 was shrinking. Right now it's at a record.
Twelve months after that pullback, Bitcoin was up 242%. That's what this moment looked like last time.

facts.text: Early 2023: BTC low 15,787 on Nov 21 2022, up 57% to 24,829 on Feb 20, back down 18.7% to 20,187 on Mar 10. 12 months later: 69,020, up 242%
2026: BTC low 58,559 on Jun 30, up 48% to 86,603 on Sep 21, back down 12.3% to 75,942 on Nov 5. The Nov 1 weekly close was 2.0% above the top of the 20-week SMA and 21-week EMA band
M2 year over year: -3.85% in March 2023, +5.71% in September 2026, at a record

careful: You reject the four-year cycle, so keep this about the move and the liquidity, never the calendar. It is one precedent, so say 'last time', never 'this time it will'.
These numbers move. Re-read the live price and Sunday's weekly close on record day.
tabs.show: We are here: add the 20-week SMA and 21-week EMA, scroll to Feb and Mar 2023, circle it with the brush, then come back to this week.

tabs.label: Fear and Greed Index
tabs.show: Hover the chart back to August, then read today's number.
prompts: A few weeks ago everybody was euphoric. Now look at this. A 12% drop is all it took.

facts.text: The alternative.me index went from 78 on Sep 22 to 28 on Nov 6. CoinMarketCap's own index read 31 on Nov 6, with a yearly high of 82 on Aug 27

careful: Read the number off your tab. Do not say fear means buy: Fear alone is not a timing signal. Since 2018, on days the alternative.me index was at 31 or lower, BTC 90 days later had a median of -2.0% and was up 48% of the time, against +3.5% and 54% on all days. A year later: +31% and 61%, against +41% and 65%.
inspiring: You've looked at old charts and asked how anybody didn't buy there. Well, this is what it feels like. You're inside one of those moments right now, and it never feels good.
The people on the sidelines will always find a reason to stay on the sidelines.

topics.title: The money supply just hit a record
topics.why_now: M2 is at a record 23.4 trillion, even with the Fed's holdings nearly flat since July.
topics.angle: This is your liquidity thesis on one slide. The Fed shrank and the money still grew, so the fuel for a bull run does not depend on the Fed alone.

tabs.label: Same QT. Opposite result.
prompts: People keep saying the money is drying up. Look at this. The money supply just hit a record.
The Fed shrank by 2.2 trillion dollars and M2 still grew. That's the fuel for everything we're about to talk about.

facts.text: M2 is at a record $23.4T in September 2026, up 5.7% from a year earlier
June 2022 to November 2025: Fed securities -$2,233B, bank credit +$1,851B, M2 +$622B
facts.source: computed from FRED WSHOSHO, TOTBKCR, M2SL

careful: The Fed's bill buying is called reserve management, not QE, and its holdings are nearly flat since July, so say M2, not 'the Fed is printing'.

topics.title: Quant: the layer the banks are letting into the building
topics.why_now: QNT went from 56 in August to 286 in September, and The Clearing House network it was picked for has a date: the first half of 2027.
topics.angle: Give Quant holders their moment in two tabs: the chart that woke everybody up, and the release that explains why. Then move on to Kaspa.

tabs.label: QNT weekly on TradingView
prompts: I don't own any Quant myself, but I think it could do very well. Let me show you why.
Look at May 2021. Quant had just gone up 467%, then it dropped 49% in five days. That felt like the end. Four months later it was at 394.
Now look at this year. Up 412% from the August low, down 34% from the high. We are here.
And there are only around 14.6 million QNT in the entire world.

facts.text: 2021: QNT low 10.79 on Dec 23 2020, up 467% to 61.19 on May 18, down 49% to 31.44 in 5 days, then 393.54 on Sep 10 2021
Total supply 14,612,493 QNT

careful: 2021 was a market-wide bull run, so say 'last time', never 'this time it will'.
tabs.show: We are here: add the 50-week and 200-week SMA, scroll to May 2021, circle it, then come back to this year.

tabs.label: The Clearing House picks Quant
prompts: Read this. The Clearing House is owned by 25 of the nation's largest financial institutions, and it picked Quant for the layer that connects its on-chain money network.

facts.text: TCH: 'Quant's technology will enable the network's interoperability, orchestration, and transaction-management layer', available 'in the first half of 2027'. Its existing rails 'clear and settle more than $2 trillion each day'
TCH is 'owned by 25 of the nation's largest financial institutions'
UK Finance: 'successful completion of our GBTD retail live pilots' in September 2026, on a platform 'developed by Quant'

careful: TCH selected Quant, and that $2 trillion is the existing rails. Never 'the banks picked Quant' or '$2 trillion a day runs on Quant'.
Nothing published says the bank contracts flow through QNT, so sell the contracts and the layer, not token demand.
tabs.show: Highlight the 'interoperability, orchestration, and transaction-management layer' line.
inspiring: It's not trying to become the banks' new blockchain. It's the layer the banks are actually letting into the building. Live in the UK, with a date in the US.

topics.why_now: KAS is 1.3x off its 2026 low at the Nov 4 close while Quant is more than 3x off its own, and Toccata, Silverscript and KCC-20 all shipped this year.
topics.angle: This is your coin and your conviction. Put the chart up right after Quant's and let the contrast do the work: same market, and this one has not moved yet. Keep 'is it next?' as a question.

tabs.label: KAS weekly on TradingView
prompts: Look at 2023. Kaspa ran up 805%, then it dropped 66% by May. That's the kind of drop that makes people quit. From that low it went almost 13x by February 2024, and nobody who quit was there for it.
Quant is more than 3x off its low. Kaspa is barely above its low. So you tell me: what happens when the market wakes up to this one?

facts.text: 2023: KAS low 0.0044 on Jan 7, up 805% to 0.0398 on Apr 1, down 66% to 0.0134 on May 23, then 0.1837 on Feb 19 2024, 13.7x from that low
Its all-time high close of 0.2056 on Jul 31 2024 is around 6x from that Nov 4 close

careful: Keep 'what happens next' a question, never a price promise. Your 3.33 target stays a target.
On Sunday closes it is back under the 50-week SMA, so skip that line unless your chart shows otherwise on record day.
tabs.show: We are here: scroll to April and May 2023, circle the drop, then come back to this year.
inspiring: I am more bullish on Kaspa now than I've ever been, and it has nothing to do with the price.
The tools came first, the crowd has not arrived yet. And that's exactly the gap where I want to be standing.

Think about everything that got built without those doors ever opening. Now imagine the conversation the day one of them does.
Kaspa's founder turned down Binance's invitation and said they're 'unfit for cypherpunk'. How many founders do you know who would do that?

topics.title: How a better coin breaks Bitcoin's network effect
topics.why_now: Kaspa's founder named the problem at the Oxford Union, and you have a theory for how it breaks.
topics.angle: The big-vision moment. Bitcoin's network effect is the wall, your cascade is how it comes down, and Kaspa's roadmap shows it is built for it. It is your theory, so call it your theory, with full conviction.

tabs.label: Yonatan: Bitcoin's network trap
prompts: Even Kaspa's own founder says it: Bitcoin's network effect is a trap. So how does a better coin ever break out?

My long-term theory is that Ethereum eventually takes the number one spot from Bitcoin, and a lot of Bitcoin maxis are going to be looking for a proof-of-work home. I think they find Kaspa, not all at once, sort of like a cascade over time.
tabs.words: there are thousands of tokens that are launched and they can't really overcome the network effect of Bitcoin. Although there's no argument about Bitcoin being an inferior technology, and still it has a a network trap.
tabs.caption: Yonatan Sompolinsky, Kaspa founder, Oxford Union, April 2026
tabs.context: He answers a student asking whether tokens solve the network-effect trap. He is not predicting Kaspa fails and not promising it wins. What follows is a separate point, so cutting there changes nothing.
tabs.heard: There are thousands of tokens that are launched and they can't really overcome the network effect of Bitcoin, although there's no argument about Bitcoin being an inferior technology, and still it has a network trap.

topics.title: The close: why I'm still here
topics.why_now: Weeks like this are when people quit, and this is the part people remember.
topics.angle: Back to your face, back to the conviction. Send both sets of fans away fired up, without promising a price.

prompts: Follow me, because I'm going to keep showing you the receipts.
inspiring: If you hold Kaspa, you hold a coin nobody was handed and nobody owns. And if you hold Quant, you're betting on the layer the banks are actually letting in.
Nobody rings a bell at the bottom. It never feels good at the moment it matters.
You don't need a hundred coins. You need to understand one or two better than everybody else, and you need the patience to sit through weeks like this one.
I don't think we've even heard the music yet.
Five years from now nobody is going to remember this week's candle. They're going to remember who was still here.
